newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends higher on crop worries, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends higher on crop worries, weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures ended higher on Tuesday, bolstered by ideas persistent cool, wet weather would hamper early crop development, pit sources said.
"I thought the crop ratings certainly didn't support a 131 bushel yield in corn which was friendly," said Dan Cekander, analyst with FIMAT Futures.

He was referring to USDA's weekly crop update which showed the corn crop was rated eight percent excellent, 52 percent good, 33 percent fair, six percent poor and one percent very poor. Last year at this time, 51 percent was rated good to excellent, USDA said.
Cekander and others noted that while this year's ratings were better than last year, it was too early to bank on a bumper crop. USDA in May predicted corn yields at 131 bushels per acre.
"You can plant early but if it lays there in the ground and doesn't germinate, it doesn't do any good," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter.
Long range forecasts offered little hope for a warm-up with temperatures expected to stay below normal next week.
Corn ended 3-1/2 to 1-1/2 cent per bushel higher with July up 3-1/2 at $2.77-1/2.
Technical signals triggered late fund buying in the July. Traders said Rosenthal Collins bought at least three million bushels July on the close.

On the day, commercials were on both sides of the market. Cargill Inc bought three million bushels July and Continental Grain bought two million July but ADM sold one million July and Term Commodities sold five million July.
Funds were also split but most were said to be buyers late. Prudential Securities sold 1.5 million July and bought one million December, traders said.
Options were a key factor, sparking bullish interest in the December, traders said.
Farmers Commodities Corp was said to be the largest player of the day. FCC bought 2,500 September $2.40 puts and 2,500 September $2.20 puts, and sold 5,000 $2.30 puts at 1-1/4 cents, traders said.
Floor sources termed the move a "butterfly" spread.

"It is a relatively low-risk, inexpensive way to capitalize if the market goes lower, with the maximum profit realized at $2.30," one options trader said. "It's a fairly common bearish move but the volume is unusually large."
Traders said FIMAT Futures bought 1,400 July $2.80 puts at 8-1/2 to eight cents and Lind-Waldock sold 1,600 December $2.50 puts at 11 cents.
Corn futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 45,000 contracts, just under Monday's actual volume of 45,375.
